```json
{"claims":[{"claim_text":"Most of organized labor and the immigrant rights and Latino advocacy community critically support the Senate-passed S 744 — the Border Security, Economic Opportunity, and Immigration Modernization Act of 2013 — because it provides a path to citizenship for millions of undocumented workers.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Organized labor, the immigrant rights community, and the Latino advocacy community are pushing for the House to take up the Senate bill.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Democratic Socialists of America understands the decision of organized labor and the immigrant rights and Latino advocacy community to support the Senate bill.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Democratic Socialists of America will work with the National Network for Immigrant and Refugee Rights (NNIRR) and grassroots groups who raise fundamental questions about the Senate bill because it promises to further militarize the border and increase the harassment of borderlands communities.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The Senate bill promises to further militarize the border.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The Senate bill will increase the harassment of borderlands communities.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The Senate bill provides an arduous 13-year path to citizenship for the large majority — but not all — of the approximately 11 million undocumented workers.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The Senate bill would grant legal status to millions of immigrants and their dependents.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The Senate bill would allow immigrants and their dependents to work and travel without fear of deportation.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Immigrants embarking on the lengthy road to citizenship under the Senate bill cannot go more than 60 days without employment.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The 60-day employment restriction in the Senate bill would severely hamper immigrants from defending their rights in the workplace.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The minimum of $3,750 in fees during the path to citizenship under the Senate bill will put full citizenship out of the reach of many.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[2]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
